title: Passive 2 (be done / been done / being done)
subtitle: be done / been done / being done
summary: Form the passive after modal verbs, in the perfect tenses and in the continuous tenses: will be done, has been done, is being done.

lesson.heading: Infinitive: (to) be done
lesson.text: Active: (to) do/clean/see etc. Passive: **(to) be + done/cleaned/seen** etc. We use this after will, must, can, could, going to and after verbs like want.

examples.text: Somebody will clean this room later. → This room **will be cleaned** later.
The situation is serious. Something **must be done** before it's too late.
A mystery is something that **can't be explained**.
The music was very loud and **could be heard** from a long way away.
A new supermarket **is going to be built** next year.
Please go away. I want **to be left** alone.

lesson.heading: Perfect infinitive: (to) have been done
lesson.text: Active: (to) have + done/cleaned/seen etc. Passive: **(to) have been + done/cleaned/seen** etc. We use this after should, might, would etc. when we talk about the past.

examples.text: Somebody should have cleaned the room. → The room **should have been cleaned**.
I haven't received the letter yet. It **might have been sent** to the wrong address.
If you had locked the car, it **wouldn't have been stolen**.
There were some problems at first, but they seem **to have been solved**.

lesson.heading: Present perfect: have/has been done
lesson.text: Active: have/has + done etc. Passive: **have/has been + done** etc.

examples.text: The room looks nice. Somebody has cleaned it. → The room looks nice. It **has been cleaned**.
Have you heard? The trip **has been cancelled**.
**Have** you ever **been bitten** by a dog?
'Are you going to the party?' 'No, **I haven't been invited**.'

lesson.heading: Past perfect: had been done
lesson.text: Active: had + done etc. Passive: **had been + done** etc.

examples.text: The room looked nice. Somebody had cleaned it. → The room looked nice. It **had been cleaned**.
The vegetables didn't taste good. They **had been cooked** too long.
The car was three years old, but **hadn't been used** very much.

lesson.heading: Present and past continuous: is being done / was being done
lesson.text: Present continuous active: am/is/are + (do)ing. Passive: **am/is/are + being (done)**. Past continuous active: was/were + (do)ing. Passive: **was/were + being (done)**.

examples.text: Somebody is cleaning the room at the moment. → The room **is being cleaned** at the moment.
There's somebody walking behind us. I think we **are being followed**.
A new bridge **is being built** across the river. It will be finished next year.
Somebody was cleaning the room when I arrived. → The room **was being cleaned** when I arrived.
There was somebody walking behind us. I think we **were being followed**.

lesson.text: Keep the tense of the active sentence and change only the verb: has cleaned becomes has been cleaned, is cleaning becomes is being cleaned.

exercises.prompt: The situation is serious. Something ___ before it's too late.
exercises.explanation: After a modal verb (must) the passive is be + past participle: must be done.

exercises.prompt: These documents are important. They should always ___ in a safe place.
exercises.explanation: After should, the passive infinitive is be + past participle: should be kept.
Present perfect passive: has been + past participle. The bike didn't steal anything.

exercises.prompt: This road is in bad condition. It should ___ a long time ago.
exercises.explanation: A long time ago is past, so use the perfect infinitive passive: should have been repaired.

exercises.prompt: Which passive form is used in each sentence?

items.text: Have you heard? The trip has been cancelled.
A new bridge is being built across the river.
The vegetables had been cooked too long.
I think we are being followed.
The car hadn't been used very much.

exercises.prompt: A friend of mine was stung by a bee recently. Ask your friend about their experience. (you / ever / sting / bee?)
exercises.answer: Have you ever been stung by a bee?
exercises.explanation: Present perfect passive question: Have + subject + ever + been + past participle.

exercises.statement: You can't use the bathroom now. The room is cleaning at the moment.
exercises.explanation: The room is being cleaned at the moment. Present continuous passive is am/is/are + being + past participle.

exercises.prompt: The bridge was damaged recently. It ___ at the moment.
exercises.explanation: At the moment means the action is in progress now: present continuous passive (is being repaired).

exercises.prompt: I wonder how Jessica is these days. I ___ her for ages.
exercises.explanation: I am the one who sees, so the verb is active: I haven't seen her. Compare: He hasn't been seen since then.

exercises.prompt: I didn't know that somebody was recording our conversation. Write the sentence in the passive.
exercises.answer: I didn't know that our conversation was being recorded.
exercises.explanation: Past continuous passive: was/were + being + past participle.

exercises.prompt: It's not certain how the fire started. It might ___ by an electrical fault.
exercises.explanation: The fire is past, so after might we need the perfect infinitive passive: might have been caused.

exercises.statement: The vegetables didn't taste good. They had been cooked too long.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Past perfect passive (had been cooked) for something that happened before they tasted them.
